linkedIssues.title: [Bug]: Generic error toasts still show raw "HTTP request failed (<status>): {json}" text (settings save, MCP delete, shared links)
criteria:
- [ ] For an SDK `HttpError`, a toast built by `retrieveAxiosErrorMessage` (in the global `QueryCache`/`MutationCache` handler or another caller) shows the server's message, never the `HTTP request failed (...)` text. This holds for a string `message`, `detail` or `error` in the body and for FastAPI validation `detail` arrays.
- [ ] An SDK `HttpError` without a usable body shows the caller's localized fallback (`ERROR$GENERIC` in the global handlers).
- [ ] Axios errors, plain `Error`s and strings keep their current messages, including the "Disconnected (...)" wording for network failures and timeouts.
- [ ] Flows 1-4 show the expected text on a running stack.
- [ ] A toast built by the global `QueryCache.onError` / `MutationCache.onError` handlers for an SDK `HttpError` shows the server's message, never the `HTTP request failed (<status> <statusText>): {json}` transport text. This holds for a string `message`, `detail`, or `error` field in the body and for a FastAPI validation `detail` array.
- [ ] A toast built by any `retrieveAxiosErrorMessage` caller under `src/` for an SDK `HttpError` shows the server's message, never the transport text.
- [ ] An SDK `HttpError` without a usable body yields the caller's localized fallback (`ERROR$GENERIC`, i.e. `An error occurred`, in the global handlers), not the transport text.
- [ ] Axios errors, plain `Error`s, and strings keep their current messages, including the "Disconnected (check URL or network)." and "Disconnected (request timed out)." wording for network failures and timeouts.
- [ ] On a running stack, flows 1-4 from Steps to Reproduce show the Expected Behavior text: `Settings validation failed`; `MCP server 'qa_stale' was not found`; `Not Found`; and `An error occurred` for the plain-text 502 body.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the `HttpError` body variants (`message`, `detail`, `error`, FastAPI validation array, no usable body) and the preserved axios / `Error` / string behavior, following the Arrange/Act/Assert style of `__tests__/utils/api-error-message.test.ts`.

linkedIssues.title: [Feature]: Repository-local feature map and weekly main verification skills
criteria:
- [ ] Repo-local skill(s) have valid AgentSkills metadata and a discoverable feature-map index with stable IDs, user entry points, source anchors, safe prerequisites, action/result recipes and gotchas.
- [ ] Instructions cover real launch, doctor, browser driving, evidence and owned-process cleanup; execute at least one mapped feature end to end on current main and retain reviewed proof after teardown.
- [ ] Weekly verification freezes BASE/TARGET and handles incomplete history; reconciles changed paths and associated merged PRs with explicit intent evidence, including unknown/contradictory intent.
- [ ] Runtime pass/fail/blocked/not-run is separate from intent and regression attribution. Cloud, ACP, native-platform and external-account gaps cannot silently count as passes.
- [ ] Desktop/mobile inspection, native password masking with dummy values, reload persistence and browser exceptions are covered; prior evidence/baselines are never silently replaced.
- [ ] Product bugs are reported separately from map/harness drift. No production settings, application behavior, schedule, paid model call or remote integration is changed by the basic rehearsal.
- [ ] Existing `qa-changes`, the release testing matrix, repository boundaries and human-only PR sections remain respected; no recurring automation is deployed by this change.
- [ ] A repo-local skill under `.agents/skills/` has valid AgentSkills frontmatter (`name`, `description`, `triggers` consistent with existing `release.md` / `pr-design-doc` / `custom-codereview-guide.md`) and is discoverable/invokable by a fresh agent (via an `AGENTS.md` or `.agents` pointer).
- [ ] A feature-map index with stable per-feature IDs exists as `features/README.md` (or equivalent) plus one file per seed feature (top 3–5), each answering: user entry point, how to reach it from the user's POV, how to drive it with the chosen harness, and what observable end state proves it works; source anchors, safe prerequisites, action/result recipes, and gotchas are populated (no placeholders).
- [ ] The skill's `Launch` names the exact command from the repo's own launchers and how to detect readiness (log line / port); `Doctor` is a read-only check; `Drive` uses real selectors/commands; `Evidence` states the proof standard and artifact location; `Cleanup` removes only the processes the run started (by tracked descriptor, not process name) and preserves evidence.
- [ ] The generated skill is proven end-to-end once on current `main`: launch → doctor → drive at least one mapped feature in a real browser → capture evidence → teardown → confirm the evidence survives teardown; evidence (screenshots/transcript/response bodies) is retained at a reviewable PR location.
- [ ] Weekly main-verification instructions freeze `BASE` and `TARGET` and handle incomplete/detail history (e.g. `git log --oneline TARGET --not BASE` empty, or a shallow clone) without reporting results it could not compute.
- [ ] The procedure maps changed source paths to associated merged PRs and requires explicit intent evidence per PR (title/description, linked issue, or reviewer comment); unknown or contradictory intent, or a change with no associated PR, is recorded and reported rather than guessed.
- [ ] Runtime outcome is classified separately from intent and regression attribution: each changed path is reported exactly one of `pass / fail / blocked / not-run`, and Cloud, ACP, native-platform, and external-account gaps cannot count as `pass`.
- [ ] Desktop/mobile viewport inspection, native password masking with dummy values, reload persistence, and browser-exception capture are each represented in the seed map or instructions; prior evidence/baselines are never silently replaced (any replacement preserves the prior artifact or is explicitly versioned).
- [ ] Product bugs / runtime defects are reported distinctly from map/harness drift, and only demonstrably proven map/harness corrections are proposed (no speculative product code changes).
- [ ] The basic rehearsal is non-mutating: no production settings, application behavior, schedule, paid model call, or remote integration changes as a side effect (mock/test/do-no-track paths, using the in-repo mock-LLM and mock-ACP servers).
- [ ] `qa-changes` retains its existing boundary (reused unchanged, no semantic redefinition) and `docs/TESTING_MATRIX.md`, `tests/e2e/mock-llm/**`, `tests/e2e/live/**`, and the live-E2E rule ("never part of `npm run test:e2e`") stay untouched.
- [ ] No recurring automation is deployed: no GitHub Actions workflow, scheduler, cron, or `OpenHands/automation` catalog entry is added by this change.

criteria:
- [ ] Composer `+` tools menu: Escape closes it (no `tools-context-menu`; `chat-plus-button` has `aria-expanded="false"`) and focus returns to `chat-plus-button`, also when focus was on an item in the menu.
- [ ] Status-dot menu opened with a click or with Enter on the focused dot: Escape closes it (no `server-status-context-menu`) and focus returns to `server-status-menu-trigger`. Opened by hovering the dot, Escape closes it and focus stays where it was.
- [ ] Drawer tabs menu, beside the chat and on the phone panel page: Escape closes it (no `conversation-tabs-menu-*` rows) and focus returns to its ⋮ (`Customize tabs`), also when focus was on a row.
- [ ] With the context-window popover open and the status menu opened after it (steps 22-23), the first Escape closes only the status menu and the second closes the popover.
- [ ] With the command menu (Ctrl+K) opened over the `+` menu or the tabs menu, the first Escape closes only the command menu and the second closes the menu below it.
- [ ] Composer `+` tools menu: pressing Escape while it is open closes it (no `tools-context-menu`; `chat-plus-button` has `aria-expanded="false"`) and moves focus to `chat-plus-button`, including when focus was on a menu item (e.g. `macros-button`).
- [ ] Status-dot menu opened with a click or with Enter on the focused `server-status-menu-trigger`: Escape closes it (no `server-status-context-menu`) and moves focus to `server-status-menu-trigger`.
- [ ] Status-dot menu opened by hovering the dot: Escape closes it and leaves focus where it was (no focus move).
- [ ] Drawer tabs menu, on the desktop chat drawer and on the phone panel page (`/conversations/<id>/panel`): Escape closes it (no `conversation-tabs-menu-*` rows) and moves focus to its `⋮` (`Customize tabs`), including when focus was on a row.
- [ ] Layering: with the context-window popover (`context-window-meter-popover`) open and the status menu opened afterwards, the first Escape closes only the status menu (the popover stays open and `context-window-meter` does not gain focus) and a second Escape closes the popover.
- [ ] Layering: with the command menu (Ctrl+K) opened over the `+` menu or over the tabs menu, the first Escape closes only the command menu and a second Escape closes the menu below it.
- [ ] Lifecycle: after a menu is closed with Escape, reopening it and pressing Escape closes it again (no stale layer left on the stack); closing it by outside click, trigger toggle, or item selection still works and leaves no layer that a later Escape would close instead of the then-top-most popup.
- [ ] No regression: the header `⋯` menu, the Git actions menu, and the context-window popover still close on Escape and return focus to `ellipsis-button`, `conversation-git-actions-toggle`, and `context-window-meter` respectively, and no page or app errors are logged during these interactions.
- [ ] Validation in the running app: the issue's reproduction steps produce the expected results on a build containing the fix, driven with `control-openhands` (or an equivalent manual pass), with no page or app errors (`browser errors --app-only`); regression tests cover Escape for the three menus and the layering cases, and `npm test`, `npm run lint`, and `npm run build` pass.

criteria:
- [ ] The live stack starts terminals on CI (no `File name too long` in the job log).
- [ ] Playwright exits within seconds of the last test, and the job ends `success` or `failure`, never `cancelled` by the job timeout.
- [ ] The critic spec reaches the proxy's critic endpoint (`/vllm/classify`).
- [ ] With #18081 fixed, a `main` push (or `workflow_dispatch` on the fix PR) produces a green `live-e2e` job.

- [ ] The Agent Server receives a tmux socket directory whose socket path fits the 108-byte Unix limit at the CI checkout path, and an operator-provided `TMUX_TMPDIR` is still honored rather than overridden.
- [ ] After the last spec, Playwright prints its summary and the process exits within seconds without an orphaned `openhands-agent-server` holding its pipes; the `live-e2e` job ends `success` or `failure`, never `cancelled` by its 30-minute timeout.
- [ ] The critic spec sends its evaluation to the proxy's critic route (`…/vllm/classify`), not `…/classify`, and a non-404 response from that route is observed in the run.
- [ ] Both specs run and each reports its own result: a passing run shows both green, and a failing run surfaces the failure with a non-zero job exit code inside the timeout.
- [ ] With #18081 fixed, a `main` push (or `workflow_dispatch` on the fix PR) produces a green `live-e2e` job.
- [ ] Live credentials stay out of job-level `env` and out of logs/artifacts: the LLM key is injected only into the step that runs the test.

linkedIssues.title: [Feature]: Repository-local feature map and weekly main verification skills
criteria:
- [ ] Repo-local skill(s) have valid AgentSkills metadata and a discoverable feature-map index with stable IDs, user entry points, source anchors, safe prerequisites, action/result recipes and gotchas.
- [ ] Instructions cover real launch, doctor, browser driving, evidence and owned-process cleanup; execute at least one mapped feature end to end on current main and retain reviewed proof after teardown.
- [ ] Weekly verification freezes BASE/TARGET and handles incomplete history; reconciles changed paths and associated merged PRs with explicit intent evidence, including unknown/contradictory intent.
- [ ] Runtime pass/fail/blocked/not-run is separate from intent and regression attribution. Cloud, ACP, native-platform and external-account gaps cannot silently count as passes.
- [ ] Desktop/mobile inspection, native password masking with dummy values, reload persistence and browser exceptions are covered; prior evidence/baselines are never silently replaced.
- [ ] Product bugs are reported separately from map/harness drift. No production settings, application behavior, schedule, paid model call or remote integration is changed by the basic rehearsal.
- [ ] Existing `qa-changes`, the release testing matrix, repository boundaries and human-only PR sections remain respected; no recurring automation is deployed by this change.
- [ ] A repo-local skill under `.agents/skills/` has valid AgentSkills frontmatter (`name`, `description`, `triggers` consistent with existing `release.md` / `pr-design-doc` / `custom-codereview-guide.md`) and is discoverable/invokable by a fresh agent (via an `AGENTS.md` or `.agents` pointer).
- [ ] A feature-map index with stable per-feature IDs exists as `features/README.md` (or equivalent) plus one file per seed feature (top 3–5), each answering: user entry point, how to reach it from the user's POV, how to drive it with the chosen harness, and what observable end state proves it works; source anchors, safe prerequisites, action/result recipes, and gotchas are populated (no placeholders).
- [ ] The skill's `Launch` names the exact command from the repo's own launchers and how to detect readiness (log line / port); `Doctor` is a read-only check; `Drive` uses real selectors/commands; `Evidence` states the proof standard and artifact location; `Cleanup` removes only the processes the run started (by tracked descriptor, not process name) and preserves evidence.
- [ ] The generated skill is proven end-to-end once on current `main`: launch → doctor → drive at least one mapped feature in a real browser → capture evidence → teardown → confirm the evidence survives teardown; evidence (screenshots/transcript/response bodies) is retained at a reviewable PR location.
- [ ] Weekly main-verification instructions freeze `BASE` and `TARGET` and handle incomplete/detail history (e.g. `git log --oneline TARGET --not BASE` empty, or a shallow clone) without reporting results it could not compute.
- [ ] The procedure maps changed source paths to associated merged PRs and requires explicit intent evidence per PR (title/description, linked issue, or reviewer comment); unknown or contradictory intent, or a change with no associated PR, is recorded and reported rather than guessed.
